doc.title: Jimmy and Jeannie Cheatham interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 12, 1998

chapter: Papa Jo Jones and the Sweet Baby Blues Band
title: Sweet Baby Blues Band members past and present
summary: Jeannie names the original Sweet Baby Blues Band, John Harris the drummer admired by Jo Jones, Ed Thigpen and Roy Haynes, and the new band members.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Well you guys sound like maybe you are or could become the Milt and Mona Hinton of the San Diego area.
Oh, I don’t know.
I mean there’s certain people that you like to be around. Because they give what you guys are talking about.
That’s why the Sweet Baby Blues Band was so special.
Really.

It was Curtis Peagler, Red Callender, Jimmy Noone, see and John Harris. Now John Harris is the only one left from our old group. You know he played with Carmen McRae, he played with Horace Silver, and quite a few. And he’s one of the most sensitive drummers. Jo Jones was crazy about him.
And so was Ed.
Ed Thigpen.
Ed Thigpen. And Roy Haynes even liked him.

Roy Haynes loved him, you know, because both of them came up to the Vine Street Grill when we were playing, and they were just sitting there checking out John. He said be sure, I want to meet him, have him come to my table. Because he says I don’t believe what I’m seeing and hearing simultaneously. He said I haven’t seen this in years. A drummer, the way he is comping and playing and expressing.

And he can catch a trumpet player in mid-air. He can tell whether he’s going to split a note or not. He hits his bass drum, and then the note just comes out of the trumpet. That’s the way Papa Jo was.
Yeah, Papa Jo was. And I don’t know —
Use certain cymbals and do the same thing, or whatever.
And he walks around in their heads.

And he knows. And that’s where he’s such a valuable accompanist. And I could see why Carmen McRae would love him, see because we worked with her too. But he’s the last one of the old band. In our new band now we have Ricky Woodard, we have Nolan Shaheed, we have Richard Reid on bass. We call him “Roughouse.” And we express to the audience, if you don’t behave we’re going to let Richard Reid fall on you.
I take it he’s a fairly big man.
He’s a big guy.
He comes in the door sideways.
He comes in the door sideways?
Well he got his face through—
He’s a big old guy.
But then there’s the one gigantic—
And we have Ernie Fields. Now Ernie Fields played baritone and also —
Bass clarinet. And clarinet.
And clarinet. But he and his dad were both put into the Hall of Fame in Oklahoma — the first time they ever had a father and son combination in Oklahoma.
